    Left-end hooks and cohooks for string modules #

    Butler--Ringel's canonical exact sequences use hook and cohook operations at both ends of a string. Reversal exchanges the two endpoints, so the left-end operations are obtained from the already constructed right-end operations. The module maps are transported through the canonical reversal isomorphisms; no second coordinate calculation is needed.
